pattern_scope: Search exact API-family literal in all retained bytes, including static C-name/link_name/JIT lookup strings.
Find simple object-like macro aliases, function-pointer/symbol assignments, import renames, Cython external C-name bindings, function-like forwarding/replacement macros.
Find C/C++ brace-delimited and Cython/Python function wrapper bodies; record Python code-generation/JIT binding strings separately.
Scan every retained file in affected packages for names of discovered aliases/wrappers; retain references/callback function addresses as candidates, not automatic calls.
limitations: This is a heuristic static alias/caller discovery, not a compiler or whole-program analysis; callers require owner verification.
No arbitrary transitive semantic wrapper graph is automatically counted. Direct constructor/wrapper definitions and arguments must be inspected.

Cannot prove dynamically computed symbol names, dlsym/GetProcAddress strings assembled at runtime, preprocessor token pasting unrelated to literal API roots, or aliases absent from retained source catalog.
C/C++ function-boundary heuristics can miss decorated/complex signatures or classify complex initializers as functions; every root is a candidate, not verified wrapper.
Only files retained by previous source recovery are available; ordinary Python files without Unicode/native indicators may be absent. All supported native source files were retained.

The catalog-wide pass searches static API-name roots, not arbitrary aliases whose names are dynamically constructed. The caller pass resolves one-hop names within each package, with manual exclusion of distinct C translation-unit/local symbols; it does not establish a compiler-validated transitive call graph.
review_method: Exact retained-source SHA256 and LF-line comparison; manually inspect distinct local/static symbols, prototypes, numeric-only dtype branches, and known generated helper/function boundaries. Wrapper calls/address references are supporting traces and never added to direct API call counts.
